content.text: The digital product economy is structurally unfair to creators in restricted markets. The tools that Western creators take for granted — Stripe for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-what-nobody-tells-2|Payment Infrastructure]]s, Gumroad for storefront and delivery, PayPal for international transfers — are either unavailable or functionally broken for creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, and dozens of other markets. The answer is not finding a better platform. The answer is removing the platform layer entirely. A sovereign digital commerce stack gives you a storefront you host, a payment processor that runs on blockchain rails, and an [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/get-automated-ebook-delivery-after-crypto-payment-working|automated]] delivery system that sends your product within 30 seconds of payment confirmation. You collect revenue directly into a wallet you control. You convert to local currency through P2P exchanges at near-market rates. The platform cannot suspend you because you are not on any platform.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-automated-digital-product-4. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Github pages

This infrastructure solution is built on GitHub Pages, a free static site hosting service that enables digital creators to host their online stores without relying on Stripe or other payment platforms. By leveraging GitHub Pages, creators can maintain full control over their digital products and customer data, avoiding platform restrictions and fees. The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) offers complete documentation for all 5 stacks, full source code, NOWPayments integration guide, and scaling playbook, providing creators with a comprehensive solution for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-deploying-digital-store-cloudflare-pages-free-works-8|COREMERCH guide to deploying]] their own sovereign digital commerce infrastructure.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture behind GitHub Pages for digital product store hosting involves using GitHub Pages for static site hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment verification. This setup allows creators to host their online stores on GitHub Pages, process payments through NOWPayments, and manage orders and customer data using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. The fees associated with NOWPayments are significantly lower than those of Gumroad, making it an attractive option for digital creators.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase.
Digital creators who want to maintain full control over their digital products and customer data can achieve significant cost savings by leveraging GitHub Pages and NOWPayments.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The key components of this infrastructure solution include GitHub Pages for static site hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment verification, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage. These components work together to enable creators to host their online stores, process payments, and manage orders and customer data, all while maintaining full control and flexibility.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy this infrastructure solution today, creators can follow these concrete steps: purchase the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or Edge Commerce Stack ($197) package, which includes deployment of the stack, 30-day support, and access to the Sovereign Blueprint ($47) documentation. Once deployed, creators can load their digital products, configure NOWPayments, and begin selling their products online. Shop for the Sovereign Starter Stack at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Is hosting on GitHub Pages free?

Selling digital products without PayPal or Stripe is not a compromise — it is an upgrade for creators in restricted markets. The conventional platforms that seem like the standard path come with payout delays, geographic restrictions, platform fees of 5 to 10 percent, and the permanent risk of account suspension. A sovereign stack has none of these constraints. Your product page loads on Cloudflare Pages. Your buyer pays in USDT or Bitcoin through a NOWPayments checkout with live price feeds and QR code generation. Your backend verifies the payment on-chain and sends the download link within 30 seconds.
By deploying a sovereign digital commerce infrastructure using GitHub Pages and NOWPayments, creators can avoid platform restrictions and fees associated with Stripe and other payment platforms.

How does GitHub Pages compare to Netlify in terms of features and pricing?

GitHub Pages offers a free static site hosting service with no limits on bandwidth or storage, while Netlify offers a paid service with more advanced features and scalability options. Both services offer a free tier with limited features, but GitHub Pages is a more cost-effective option for digital creators who want to host their online stores without relying on Stripe or other payment platforms.
Can I use GitHub Pages to host a blog or other type of digital content?

Yes, GitHub Pages can be used to host a variety of digital content, including blogs, portfolios, and other types of static websites. However, this post focuses specifically on using GitHub Pages for digital product store hosting.
